speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development what has been the take-up rate of the Lasting Power of Attorney since its introduction and how can the application process be made more accessible for citizens to sign up for it.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) is a legal instrument which allows an individual to plan ahead and appoint a trusted person to make decisions for him should he lose mental capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The take-up rate has risen after we made it easier and more convenient to make an LPA in late 2014.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Some of the changes made in late-2014 include simplification of the LPA Forms and reduction of legal terminology that are hard to understand.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: With this, the public no longer need to visit the Office of the Public Guardian to submit the forms.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We very much would like to take the opportunity to encourage more Singaporeans to make an LPA.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We also encourage the public to continue to give us feedback, so that we can continue to improve that process to make it a lot more user-friendly.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: We will continue to improve the process to make sure that the necessary safeguards are still in place.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I note the number, which is 20,000, who have applied.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Certainly, I think the LPA is a useful instrument.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Because if you look at the pool that we are trying to target, I would say that every one of us should actually do an LPA.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Put in that light, I think 20,000 is a very small number.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I think there is a lot of work that needs to be done.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I have done a dialogue on LPA with my residents and, from the questions that were asked, I think it is quite clear that many are not aware of it.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: On the process, I hear the Minister saying that the Ministry is trying to make it simpler, faster and more accessible.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I urge for a lot more efforts to be put into this and, if possible, to also set specific targets, so that there is a clear game plan and, hopefully, a year from now, this 20,000 will Page: 10 be a much bigger number.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With ease of application, it is always a balance of making it easy and also safeguarding the interest of the individuals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Because we are very mindful as individuals apply for the LPA, we also need to make sure that due diligence is applied, so that there is no undue pressure, there is no external influence.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something that we are also concerned about, with adults growing older, when mental capacities degenerate at some point and they become vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do urge every Member of this House to actively encourage and raise awareness.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will, on our part, also try to see what we can do to increase the publicity and to make sure it is as accessible as possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Indeed, this is something that most, if not all of us, should seriously consider taking up.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I do agree with the Minister and I would like to ask the Minister what would be the top three barriers to having a higher take-up rate for this very important instrument.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: What is being done to address these barriers, especially on how much more aggressive can we be?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Could we be a bit more aggressive to help, especially those who are less educated and those who are less aware?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something relatively new even though it has been introduced for a few years now.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is not something that is second nature to many of us.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I am not sure many people are also necessarily fully aware.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is something that we need to get past that stage.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: One of the other factors is I think a lot of people talk about Singaporeans being under-insured.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We sometimes do not take up enough life insurance.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I do not know whether it is because we are "pantang" or whether we try not to think about the inevitable.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But at some point, we will all degenerate as we grow older physically, mentally.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, this is something that we know is necessary.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Intellectually, many of us grasp it, but I am not sure whether we, emotively, fully hoist it on board.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It could also be that some think that by taking that step, are we also sort of acknowledging that we may at some stage reach that particular condition?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What we need to do more of is publicity to make sure that the information gets out as far as possible and that is where we would ask everyone to chip in to make sure that the residents are aware.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As I have said, we have to strike that balance.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are very mindful of that, to make sure that their individual well-being is catered for but, at the same time, to make the process easy.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are quite happy to improve the process.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, see what steps can be taken, so that they do not even need to go down specifically to submit the form.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, for them to be able to mail it in, so on and so forth.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These are steps that we will endeavour to try to make it more accessible.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Page: 11 For the less educated, it is the same thing, it is about education and awareness, how to make it more easily understandable in terms of collaterals, but this is where it is better through the grassroots organisations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We know that there are particular areas where there are older Singaporeans, lower income, perhaps, less educated.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, we may perhaps encourage more targeted efforts in those specific geographical areas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Therefore, I am wondering whether the Ministry can consider doing something like what MOH is doing with MediShield Life, having a one-on-one counselling session kind of thing for those who are in that category and they have elderly with dementia and all that, where they can do that with maybe an outsourced partner, community partners or VWO.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Because I think that is really quite helpful.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For the whole ageing package, not just with the LPA, this is something that we have been talking a lot about.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: From MOH's and our perspective, as a whole nation, there is really quite a significant range of issues related to ageing.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The volumes are going to be quite significant 10, 15 years from now.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do need to think about how to put in more resources to do this and we will take that suggestion on board.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I wanted to ask the Minister what is the average age of the individuals when they apply for LPA currently in our database.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: And, as Assoc Prof Fatimah has suggested, when they reach a certain age, such information could be mailed to the individuals or all Singaporeans when they are at a particular age, so that they know how to apply.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: On the point about the PGO playing that role – that is something that is useful.
